What We Do

Six services. Two countries. One standard of preparation.

Every case starts the same way: we measure your profile against the published criteria for that visa, tell you plainly where it is weak, and only then build the file. Pick a service to see how yours is assessed.

Please note: Borderway International is a consultancy. The final visa decision is always made by the embassy / immigration authority (IRCC, US Embassy) — we never promise a guaranteed visa. What we promise is a file prepared accurately, against the official criteria.

01

Visit / Tourist Visa

USA B1/B2 and Canada Visitor Visa (TRV). The officer's real questions are purpose, funds and ties to Pakistan — so we build the itinerary, bank evidence and ties documentation around exactly those three, in the order an officer reads them.

Business Visa

Meetings, conferences, trade fairs and exhibitions in the USA or Canada. We document the business itself — registration, tax records, company statements — and tie the trip to a specific event with an invitation or registration proof, because a vague purpose is the most common reason these are refused.

Family & Super Visa

For parents and grandparents visiting family in Canada, and family visits to the USA. Super Visa files stand or fall on the host's paperwork: income at or above LICO (CAD $38,002 for a family of 2) and medical insurance of at least CAD $100,000 for one year. We check both before anything is filed.

Official Requirements — At a Glance

  • Canada — Express Entry proof of funds (IRCC): at least CAD $15,263 for a single applicant (family of 4: $28,362) — IRCC table, updated 7 July 2025. The FSW 67-point selection grid and CRS ranking apply separately.
  • Canada — Study Permit: acceptance letter from a DLI + first year's tuition + living expenses CAD $22,895 (from 1 Sep 2025, outside Quebec; $23,448 from 1 Sep 2026) + travel.
  • Canada — Super Visa: the host's (child's / grandchild's) income at or above LICO (e.g. CAD $38,002 for a family size of 2) + medical insurance of at least CAD $100,000 coverage for 1 year.
  • Canada — Visitor Visa: a clear purpose of travel, sufficient funds, and strong ties to Pakistan — the officer must be satisfied that you will return on time.
  • USA — B1/B2 Visit: under INA section 214(b), every applicant must prove their non-immigrant intent and ties to their home country — DS-160 + interview.
  • USA — F-1 Study: an I-20 from a SEVP-approved school, the SEVIS fee, funds for the first year's costs, and the intention to return after your studies.

Policy snapshot: checked against official sources on 26 November 2026. Canada figures are from IRCC (canada.ca) — the proof of funds table was last updated 7 July 2025; study permit living expenses are CAD $22,895 from 1 September 2025 and CAD $23,448 from 1 September 2026. USA criteria are per the US Department of State (travel.state.gov) and USCIS (uscis.gov). Figures can change every year — always check the latest table on canada.ca before applying, and our team will confirm the current figures in your consultation.

Common Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

How accurate is the Free Eligibility Analysis? Is it a guarantee of a visa? +
The analysis is based on the officially published requirements of Canada (IRCC — canada.ca) and the USA (travel.state.gov / uscis.gov) — for example proof of funds, study permit funds, the Super Visa's LICO and insurance conditions, and the USA's 214(b) ties test. It is honest guidance, not a guarantee: the final visa decision is always made by the embassy / immigration officer, and you should beware of anyone who guarantees a visa. A complete analysis is done by looking at your actual documents, which the team requests on WhatsApp.
My visa was refused before. Can I apply again? +
Yes, in most cases you can apply again. First we understand the reason for the refusal (the reasons in Canada's refusal letter / GCMS notes, or the USA's 214(b) slip), then we fix those weak points and make a plan to re-apply with a better file. Re-applying without fixing the reason usually does not help.
How much funds are needed for a Canada study permit? +
Per IRCC: in addition to the first year's tuition, CAD $22,895 for living expenses (from 1 September 2025, outside Quebec) plus travel costs — from 1 September 2026 the living expenses figure is $23,448. An acceptance letter from a DLI (designated learning institution) and a strong SOP / study plan are also required. Figures are updated every year; the current figures are confirmed in your consultation.
What is the criteria for Canada Express Entry / skilled work? +
For the Federal Skilled Worker Program you must first pass the 67-point selection grid (language, education, experience, age, arranged employment, adaptability); then, in the Express Entry pool, ranking is by CRS score and invitations (ITA) are issued in draws. Settlement funds must also be proven — CAD $15,263 for a single applicant (IRCC table, July 2025). In the Eligibility Analysis we assess your profile on exactly these factors.
What matters most for a USA B1/B2 visa? +
INA section 214(b): the officer presumes that every applicant wants to immigrate — you have to disprove that presumption with strong ties to Pakistan (job/business, family, property, a clear purpose and a short trip). We practise mock interviews and answers matched to your DS-160 details.
What are the conditions for a Canada Super Visa? +
The Super Visa is only for the parents and grandparents of a Canadian citizen / permanent resident. The host's household income must be at or above IRCC's LICO table, medical insurance of at least CAD $100,000 coverage (1 year) is mandatory, and an immigration medical exam is also required. Parents can stay for up to 5 years per entry.
How do I book a consultation? +
Run the Free Eligibility Analysis above — it checks your profile against the official criteria and saves your details securely, then prepares a ready-made message with your result, which you can send on WhatsApp to the team member of your choice. You can also contact us directly on the numbers given on the team cards above.
What are the fees? +
The consultancy fee depends on the type of case and the work involved; embassy / government fees are separate and go to the relevant authority. The complete fee structure is explained clearly in the first assessment — there are no hidden charges.
